@graph.name: DPI Terminology
@graph.description: Operational definitions for Digital Public Infrastructure analysis

hasDefinedTerm.name: Corrigibility
hasDefinedTerm.description: The structural capacity of those affected by a system to detect error, signal harm, and trigger correction—without incurring material loss or irreversible consequence.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Digital Public Infrastructure
hasDefinedTerm.description: Population-scale digital systems that mediate access to government services, financial systems, or essential utilities.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Open-washing
hasDefinedTerm.description: The practice of branding closed or proprietary systems as 'open' through superficial openness claims (open APIs, open specs) while keeping implementations closed.

exclusion_page_additions.description: Database of documented cases where Aadhaar authentication failures led to denial of welfare benefits, resulting in starvation deaths or severe hardship

@graph.name: How to Evaluate Digital Public Infrastructure
@graph.description: Apply the five structural tests to any population-scale digital system

step.name: Apply EXIT Test
step.text: Determine if people can refuse the system without material penalty while retaining access to equivalent government services through non-digital means.

step.name: Apply CODE Test
step.text: Verify if the complete executable source code is publicly available and inspectable, not just APIs or specifications.

step.name: Apply AUDIT Test
step.text: Check if independent parties can verify system claims (security, accuracy, fairness) without requiring permission from operators.

step.name: Apply GOVERN Test
step.text: Assess if affected populations have constitutive input into rule-making, not just consultative feedback.

step.name: Apply FORK Test
step.text: Determine if credible replacement is technically possible (code available) and legally permitted (license allows).

step.name: Evaluate Results
step.text: Failure of ANY single test means the system is not public infrastructure. Tests are binary and exclusionary—there is no partial pass.
